paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Algorithm For Robust Optimization via Stochastic-Gradient Online Learning

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical oracle-based meta-algorithm for robust convex optimization with runtime eO(((sqrt(smd)+s)T∇ + min{m,s}TP + Tϵ)/ϵ^2 · max{F, D^2(G2^2 + G1G∞ − G2^2/s)}), and shows a 3ϵ-approximation guarantee with probability at least 1−δ. Relative to the classical Ben-Tal et al. (2015) method, it claims at most quadratic improvements in m and/or d under favorable sparsity conditions, but provides no hardware experiment or empirical benchmark.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical stochastic dual-subgradient meta-algorithm for robust convex optimization, with quantum subroutines used for state preparation, ℓ1-norm estimation, and multi-sampling; applied to robust linear programs and robust semidefinite programs under ellipsoidal uncertainty.

algorithm.variant: hybrid quantum-classical online sampling-based dual subgradient robust optimization algorithm
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Run for T iterations as defined by target accuracy ϵ; returns INFEASIBLE or a 3ϵ-approximate solution with probability at least 1−δ

hyperparameters.s: number of sampled pairs per iteration

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum access to noise memory and subgradient oracle; samples from the md-dimensional gradient vector via quantum state preparation and measurement
problem_formulation.objective_function: Robust feasibility/optimization: minimize f0(x) subject to fi(x,ui)≤0 for all ui∈U, i∈[m]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Robust constraints handled by online stochastic subgradient updates on noise vectors plus projection onto U; infeasibility returned by optimization oracle Oϵ

problem_instance.description: General robust convex optimization; explicit applications to robust linear programs, robust semidefinite programs, global maximum return portfolio, and truss topology design under ellipsoidal uncertainty

dataset_specification.description: No empirical dataset; theoretical problem instances and illustrative finance/engineering examples

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical runtime and approximation analysis; no numerical benchmark experiments reported

hardware.framework: quantum circuit model / QRAM-style oracle access

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical projection oracle OP and optimization oracle Oϵ; classical subgradient oracle O∇ in baseline comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Binary search over objective value to reduce optimization to feasibility; construction of stochastic subgradient oracle from sampled gradient entries

quadratic improvement in m and d when G1G∞ is comparable to G2^2

speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical benchmark; advantage depends on sparsity/promises about ℓ1 and ℓ∞ subgradient norms. Dense instances may show no advantage.

notes: The paper is gate-based and explicitly uses the quantum circuit model with QRAM-style quantum access, quantum state preparation, quantum norm estimation, and quantum multi-sampling. No specific hardware platform, qubit count, circuit depth, or shot count is reported because the work is theoretical and oracle-based rather than an implementation on a QPU.
The paper reports only theoretical runtime improvements, not empirical quantum advantage.
The claimed speedup is conditional: quadratic improvement in m and d only when G1G∞ is comparable to G2^2; otherwise there may be no asymptotic gain.
